..
Issued at 607 AM EDT Tue Sep 15 2026

A more unsettled pattern begins today as a low pressure system (over 
Ontario) brings a warm front through our area this afternoon, and 
then a cold front this evening into the overnight hours. This cold 
front will eventually stall out as the surface low/upper forcing 
lift further into Quebec. As of this writing, better moisture 
transport is just taking aim into our area. The warm front is 
currently draped from WI (nearly occluded) south into central IL and 
into TN/KY. Expect this to lift northeast through the afternoon. I 
suspect with additional moisture moving in towards the 12-15z time 
frame that we'll see a few showers and maybe an isolated t-storm 
focused up near Lake MI initially, spreading eastward with a focus 
near the toll road. Most of the high res suggest these will 
taper off with time or even stay limited to the Lake MI area and
near Cass/Berrien/St. Joseph Co, MI. There is still ridging 
aloft and high pressure at the surface, so how much moisture 
gets into this area early will determine how the showers evolve.
The NAM is the most aggressive with this line of showers/storms
extending from northern IL/Southern WI into the thumb area of 
MI, having it continue southeastward through the morning and 
early afternoon, gradually shifting it southward as it runs into
the ridge. Other models keep it more limited and focused 
further north. For now, have pops of 20-50% for areas 
along/north of US 24, increasing with northwestward extent. Have
around 55-65% for Berrien County, MI. Don't expect any severe 
weather with this earlier activity if it survives. Right now 
from radar it looks as if the outflow is moving southeastward 
ahead of the storms, so that will certainly keep things limited 
(in addition to unfavorable timing given no 
instability/capping). SPC has our CWA in a marginal risk for 
strong- severe storms for the today/tonight period. This is a 
highly conditional threat as it will depend on how the earlier 
part of the day evolves. More showers and cloud cover in the 
west/north could limit our instability. Furthermore, the timing 
of the main cold front is slower than previous forecasts (around
00z its just southeast of Lake MI). We could see some storms 
popping around 6-8 pm ET in the west (perhaps lingering 
boundaries as well as any lake breeze could trigger things), and
if they are able to tap into decent instability we could see a 
severe threat. However, the better potential really focuses 
between 8 pm ET to Midnight as the cold front moves in while we 
have some instability and the best forcing. The main threat 
would be damaging winds (SPC has 5%), with heavy rain and 
frequent lightning. ML CAPE looks to be around 1000-1500 J/kg in
the evening (best west) and around 25-40 knots of 0-6 km bulk 
shear. Confidence is low (especially east of I 69), as we have 
potential for earlier showers/storms/cloud debris, paltry mid 
level lapse rates (5-6C/km) and the front is diminishing with 
time as it runs into the ridge. Have chances for showers and 
storms tonight in the 50-80% range. High temperatures will 
largely be in the low-mid 80s, with potential for high 80s, 
lower 90s further south and west. Heat indices look to be 95-99 
degrees for these areas as humidity increases this 
afternoon...but confidence for any kind of advisory was too low 
given limited duration and also because if the more aggressive 
NAM is correct, we could have some showers/storms/cloud cover 
that limits daytime heating. 

Shower and storm chances will persist through the weekend, with our 
lingering stalled front becoming more E-W oriented and flow aloft 
zonal to slightly troughed. This lowers overall forecast confidence 
as we are susceptible to any shortwaves that ripple through the
flow, so timing is difficult to pin down. However, for Wed-Thu,
have 50-70% chances that diminish to 20-40% Friday-Fri night. 
Additional potential returns as another cold front drops into 
the area Sat/Sat PM into early Sun, so have pops of 30-60 
percent for the most part. Highs will be in the 70s, low-mid 80s
for the majority of the period, with a couple days seeing upper
80s further south. By Sunday, highs are in the 70s. 

Moderate swim risk for Lake MI beaches in Berrien Co, MI today.
Breaking waves and currents are expected. Waves of 2-3 ft will
subside to 1-2 ft later this afternoon. There will likely be
a moderate longshore current moving south to north along the
shore (as winds shift southwest), with moderate-strong 
structural currents on the south sides of piers and breakwalls.
Rip currents are possible, but less likely given fairly shore 
parallel flow.
